observation.visible_scene: A close, static shot of two pale blue-white ice pieces resting on a wet, reddish-brown stone or brick ledge. A larger, rounded rectangular block stands tilted upright toward the right; a smaller, flatter rounded piece lies to its left. A thin sheen of water and glistening wet reflections surround their bases. The background is a softly blurred outdoor scene with trees, an open field, and a tall structure (temple/building) at the upper right.
visible_changes: Over the excerpt the upright tilted block gradually shrinks: its rounded top edge lowers and its overall height decreases from the first to the last frame, while its lean angle and horizontal position stay essentially the same (size reduction, not rotation or translation).
The smaller flat piece on the left also reduces in vertical extent, its top edge lowering so it appears to flatten slightly.
The water film and bright specular reflections around the bases persist throughout and appear to spread only marginally.
The background foliage, distant structure, and overall framing remain unchanged; no camera pan, tilt, or zoom is evident.
No new objects enter and none leave; the two ice pieces remain present in the same relative positions.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the shrinking (melting) began before the crop or continues after it is not shown.
How the two pieces came to be on the ledge, and whether the smaller left piece is a separate chunk or a fragment, is not visible.
The exact material identity of the pieces is inferred from appearance only.
uncertain_details: The magnitude of the size change is small over ~1.3 s, so precise shrinkage rates are uncertain.
Minor shifts in the glistening spots on the wet surface could be subtle changes in reflection rather than measurable water movement.
The small left object is treated as a separate ice piece, but its distinction from a reflection/fragment cannot be fully confirmed.
